interest:
I study JWST observations of high-redshift galaxies and AGN, especially
little red dots (LRDs), compact red sources, dust-reddened or broad-line AGN,
early black-hole growth, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution at cosmic dawn.

Prioritize papers about:
1. JWST/NIRCam/NIRSpec/MIRI observations of high-redshift galaxies and AGN
2. little red dots, compact red galaxies, obscured AGN, broad-line AGN, and
   high-redshift black hole candidates
3. SED fitting, spectroscopy, emission lines, photometric redshifts, stellar
   masses, dust attenuation, AGN contamination, and source classification
4. high-redshift galaxy formation, reionization-era galaxies, early SMBH
   growth, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution
5. survey papers from CEERS, JADES, UNCOVER, COSMOS-Web, PRIMER, GLASS,
   RUBIES, and similar JWST deep fields

Also keep papers about AI, machine learning, large language models (LLMs),
large multimodal models (LMMs), foundation models, anomaly detection,
automated classification, spectral/photometric inference, or research agents
when they are applied to astronomy, astrophysics, JWST data, galaxy surveys,
AGN selection, or literature/data analysis.

Deprioritize unrelated stellar, solar-system, local-universe, gravitational
wave, or purely theoretical papers unless they directly inform high-redshift
galaxies, AGN, JWST analysis, or AI-for-astronomy workflows.

papers.title: Extreme Enrichment at Cosmic Dawn: Three FeII-Strong Quasars at z > 6 from the JWST Aether survey
papers.authors: Anniek J. Gloudemans , Emanuele Paolo Farina , Roberto Decarli , Klaudia Protušová , Fabrizio Arrigoni Battaia , Eduardo Bañados , Aaron J. Barth , Silvia Belladitta , Manuela Bischetti , Hyunseop Choi , Dominika Ďurovčíková , Anna-Christina Eilers , Simona Gallerani , Thales A. Gutcke , Luca Ighina , Brian C. Lemaux , Federica Loiacono , Yoshiki Matsuoka , Chiara Mazzucchelli , Silvia Onorato , Hyewon Suh , Fabian Walter , Feige Wang , Julien Wolf , Jinyi Yang
papers.abstract: We present three outliers on the quasar main sequence at z>6, as revealed by JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations from the Aether survey, a program targeting ~200 quasars at cosmic dawn. The quasars, J0216-5226, J0320-3521, and J1429+5447, exhibit exceptionally strong FeII emission and weak H$\beta$ and [OIII] lines, indicating rapid chemical enrichment within the first Gyr of cosmic history. Their FeII strengths ($R_{\rm{FeII},\lambda4570} \equiv \rm{EW}_{\rm{FeII}}/\rm{EW}_{\rm{H}\beta}$) range between ~2.5-3.6, placing them among the top ~3% of SDSS quasars at ($0\lesssim z\lesssim 1$). The H$\alpha$ emission lines of J0216-5226 and J1429+5447 imply black hole masses of $\sim1-7\times10^9$ M$_{\odot}$ with $\lambda_{\rm{Edd}}\sim0.1-0.6$, comparable to typical high-z quasars, although virial black hole masses may be systematically overestimated in strong FeII emitters. In contrast, J0320-3521 hosts a lower mass black hole of $\sim0.2-2\times10^9$ M$_{\odot}$, suggesting possible super-Eddington rate accretion with $\lambda_{\rm{Edd}}$~0.5-6.0. The IFU data of J0320-3521 reveal a distinct emission-line region at a projected distance of ~1.5 kpc, consistent with either an interacting companion or ionized gas associated to the quasar. We further identify a complex environment around J1429+5447, including two candidate companion galaxies or extended ionized gas structures. These quasars with bright emission-line regions, J0320-3521 and J1429+5447, are radio-loud sources, while J0216-5226 remains undetected in radio ($R_{5\rm{GHz,} \,3\sigma}\lesssim4$). Together, these results confirm previous findings that highly enriched, rapidly growing black holes were already in place at cosmic dawn. Despite the small sample size, our results further highlight the diversity in environment and radio-jet properties among quasars that otherwise share the same extreme region of the quasar fundamental plane.
papers.Reasons for match: This is directly about JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of z>6 quasars, strong FeII emission, black-hole masses, Eddington ratios, and AGN environments at cosmic dawn.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks what three extreme FeII-strong quasars at z>6 reveal about early chemical enrichment and black-hole growth. It finds rapid enrichment, black-hole masses around 10^9 M_sun with a possible super-Eddington case, and companion or extended emission-line structures in some systems. This is highly relevant for my work on high-z AGN, broad-line/obscured black-hole growth, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution at cosmic dawn.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for the NIRSpec IFU emission-line measurements, especially FeII, H-beta, [OIII], and H-alpha fits
Check how virial black-hole masses and Eddington ratios are derived and what systematics are discussed for strong FeII emitters
Inspect the evidence for companion galaxies or extended ionized gas around J0320-3521 and J1429+5447
Check the radio-loudness classification and any implications for AGN feedback or environment

papers.title: Early steps in the hierarchical assembly of a Milky Way-mass galaxy 1 Gyr after the Big Bang
papers.authors: Yoshihisa Asada , Marcin Sawicki , Guillaume Desprez , Jon Judez , Marusa Bradac , Kartheik Iyer , Nicholas S. Martis , Adam Muzzin , Gael Noirot , Ghassan T. E. Sarrouh , Chris J. Willott , Jacqueline Antwi-Danso , Seiji Fujimoto , Danilo Marchesini , Vladan Markov , Luke Robbins , Visal Sok
papers.abstract: We report JWST observations of a $z_{\rm spec}=5.196$ compact group of three strongly lensed low-mass galaxies ($M_\star \sim 10^{6-7} M_\odot$ each) whose small line-of-sight velocity offsets (from $-120\pm100$ to $+160\pm110$ km s$^{-1}$) and projected separations ($\sim2$ kpc) suggest that they are undergoing merging. On the basis of abundance-matching arguments, the trio appear to be destined to evolve into a Milky Way-mass galaxy by the present day. Our spectrophotometric analysis suggests that the stellar mass growth of this system is not simply just due to the merging of its components; rather, it is being dramatically enhanced by intense bursts of star formation. Presumably initiated by tidally-induced gas inflows, these star-forming bursts boost the mass growth $2.6\pm0.5$ times that expected in straightforward merging of the existing stellar masses. These spectroscopic observations thus not only demonstrate that hierarchical assembly remains a viable formation channel in the early assembly phases of present-day massive galaxy, but also that interaction-induced bursts of star formation are a major accelerator of this assembly process.
papers.Reasons for match: This is JWST spectroscopy of a z=5.196 compact group of low-mass galaxies undergoing merging, directly relevant to early galaxy assembly, hierarchical growth, and high-redshift galaxy formation.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks whether a compact group of three low-mass galaxies at z=5.196 is undergoing merging and destined to become a Milky Way-mass galaxy. It finds small velocity offsets and projected separations consistent with merging, with interaction-induced starbursts boosting mass growth by a factor of about 2.6. This is highly relevant for my work on early galaxy assembly, JWST spectroscopy, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution at cosmic dawn.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for the NIRSpec or spectrophotometric evidence for the three components and their velocity offsets
Check the stellar-mass, star-formation-rate, and burst-fraction measurements and their uncertainties
Inspect the lensing model and how it affects the inferred sizes, masses, and separations
Check whether any AGN or black-hole growth signatures are discussed in the compact group

papers.title: Little Red Dots as a Transient Phase of Self-Interacting Dark Matter Assisted Black Hole Growth
papers.authors: Yu Rong , Shuang-Nan Zhang , Jian-Min Wang , Junxian Wang , Zhicheng He
papers.abstract: The discovery of Little Red Dots (LRDs) with JWST has revealed a population of compact, red galaxies hosting rapidly growing black holes at early cosmic times. Their compact morphologies, broad emission lines, weak X-ray emission, and distinctive V-shaped spectral energy distributions indicate a short-lived phase of black-hole growth within a dense nuclear environment. Here we propose that LRDs arise from a transient episode of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM)-assisted black-hole growth during galaxy assembly. In this scenario, gas inflows first establish a compact nuclear thick disk, which modifies the central SIDM distribution and provides the obscuring structure around the accreting black hole. Once the SIDM density near the seed black hole becomes sufficiently enhanced, rapid SIDM accretion drives a major increase in black-hole mass, initiating the transient LRD phase. The resulting obscured growth phase naturally suppresses direct short-wavelength emission and redistributes the radiation field, producing the red continuum and V-shaped spectral signatures of LRDs. This framework links gas inflow, SIDM dynamics, and early black-hole assembly, predicting that LRDs preferentially occur in galaxies undergoing strong nuclear inflow and evolve into ordinary AGN after this transient phase. Unlike models that require globally rare halo histories, long super-Eddington gas growth, or purely phenomenological obscuration, our model ties the overmassive black hole, X-ray weakness, spectral shape, and finite duty cycle to one local gas-triggered SIDM event.
papers.Reasons for match: This paper directly addresses little red dots (LRDs) as a transient phase of black-hole growth, which is central to my research on LRDs, early black-hole growth, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution at cosmic dawn.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks what physical mechanism produces the compact, red, broad-line LRDs seen by JWST. It proposes that LRDs arise from a transient episode of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM)-assisted black-hole growth, where gas inflows create a compact nuclear thick disk and enhanced SIDM density drives rapid black-hole mass growth and obscuration. This matters for my work because it offers a unified model linking LRD morphology, red continua, V-shaped SEDs, X-ray weakness, and finite duty cycles to early black-hole assembly.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for the predicted LRD duty cycle, luminosity function, and host-galaxy properties that could be compared with JWST surveys.
Check whether the model makes specific predictions for broad emission lines, X-ray weakness, or SED shape that can be tested with NIRSpec and MIRI.
Look for how the SIDM-assisted growth connects to the overmassive black-hole problem and whether it can be distinguished from super-Eddington or phenomenological obscuration models.

papers.title: A model to mini-quench early galaxies by balancing stellar feedback and gas accretion
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has discovered a population of low-mass, early galaxies with very low levels of star formation over tens of Myr. These "mini-quenched" galaxies were one of the many surprises from JWST and still require a robust explanation. We seek to explain a few important properties of these galaxies, namely the timescales governing their star formation and quenching. We use a simple model that pairs stellar feedback with the forces binding gas to a $z \sim 6$ galaxy, and with plausible parameter choices, this model produces mini-quenching in galaxies approximately as large as observed mini-quenched galaxies -- up to total stellar masses of $\sim 10^{10} M_{\odot}$. In our model, the ejected interstellar gas forms into a spherical shell that expands outward during quenching. Our novel improvement is allowing this expanding shell to prevent accreting gas from falling in, in contrast to other models whose shells do not interact with accreting gas. Using our model, if a galaxy accretes isotropically, we find that stellar feedback can reproduce observed timescales of mini-quenching with plausible galaxy-formation parameter values. However, at low halo masses, the quenching timescale of our model is too long ($> 100$ Myr). A potential solution for a long quenching time is for the galaxy to accrete via filaments, in which case only a portion of the shell interacts with the accreting gas and the quenching timescale decreases to more accepted values. However, the ram pressure from feedback cannot stop filaments with very small opening angles, as occur in some halo formation models, making mini-quenching impossible. Finally, we use this model to estimate the fraction of galaxies undergoing mini-quenching, finding that it can be large.
papers.Reasons for match: This paper directly addresses JWST-discovered low-mass early galaxies with low star formation, relevant to high-redshift galaxy formation and quenching at cosmic dawn.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks what causes the mini-quenching observed in low-mass early JWST galaxies. It proposes a model where stellar feedback drives an expanding gas shell that blocks accretion, reproducing observed quenching timescales for plausible parameters, though low-mass halos remain challenging. This matters for interpreting JWST high-z galaxy star formation histories and the role of feedback in early galaxy evolution.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for comparisons to observed JWST mini-quenched galaxy stellar masses and timescales
Check the assumptions about gas accretion geometry and filamentary inflow
Check whether predicted quenching fractions can be tested with JWST surveys
Look for any discussion of implications for reionization-era galaxy populations

papers.title: Rapid Dark Growth of Seed Black Holes in Self-Interacting Dark Matter
papers.authors: Yu Rong , Shuang-Nan Zhang , Jian-Min Wang , Junxian Wang
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of massive black holes in the early Universe, possibly related to Little Red Dots, challenges conventional growth from light seeds. Dark-matter accretion offers a distinct route, and self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) makes it possible by behaving as a collisional fluid. We show that gas inflow can drive strong local contraction of an SIDM halo, assembling a dense reservoir around a pre-existing black-hole seed. The seed then enters a rapid dark-growth phase and can gain several orders of magnitude in mass within less than $1$ Myr before transitioning to slower accretion. We self-consistently follow this process by solving the spherical Euler equations with SIDM self-gravity, collisional heat transport, and an absorbing black-hole sink, rather than imposing an accretion history. The growth depends most strongly on halo mass, with weaker sensitivity to inflowing gas fraction, nuclear size, and seed mass. Gas-inflow-driven SIDM accretion therefore provides an efficient pathway for producing massive black holes in the early Universe.
papers.Reasons for match: This paper proposes rapid dark growth of seed black holes in self-interacting dark matter, which is directly relevant to early black-hole growth and the LRD phenomenon at cosmic dawn.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks whether SIDM can enable rapid growth of seed black holes in the early Universe. It shows that gas inflow can contract an SIDM halo into a dense reservoir, allowing a seed black hole to gain several orders of magnitude in mass within less than 1 Myr before transitioning to slower accretion. This matters for my work because it provides a physical pathway for producing the massive black holes inferred from JWST LRD and high-redshift AGN observations.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for the parameter space of halo mass, seed mass, and gas fraction that produces rapid growth and whether it matches LRD host constraints.
Check whether the model predicts observable signatures such as X-ray weakness, broad lines, or compact morphologies.
Look for how the dark-growth phase ends and whether the transition to ordinary AGN is consistent with observed LRD number densities.

papers.title: MSA-3D: A Diversity of Dust Attenuation Profiles Across the Epoch of Thin Disk Emergence
papers.authors: Ivana Barišić , Tucker Jones , Naveen Reddy , Matthew Malkan , Ryan Sanders , Alaina Henry , Ayan Acharyya , Kevin Bundy , Juan M. Espejo Salcedo , Karl Glazebrook , Themiya Nanayakkara , Danail Obreschkow , Namrata Roy , Takafumi Tsukui , Benedetta Vulcani , Xin Wang
papers.abstract: We present spatially resolved measurements of dust attenuation and star formation in 18 main-sequence star-forming galaxies at z$\sim$1 from the MSA-3D survey, obtained by mapping the Balmer emission lines at $\sim$1 kpc resolution with JWST/NIRSpec's MSA in a slit-stepping strategy. We investigate the diversity of radial attenuation profiles, and how the spatial variation affects attenuation and star formation rates (SFR) derived from single-aperture measurements. We find a notable diversity among radial attenuation profiles: some galaxies exhibit centrally peaked attenuation, but the majority exhibit flat or even positive radial profiles, with large variation at a fixed stellar mass. This diversity may reflect different evolutionary pathways shaped by various mechanisms such as disk settling, merging, and internal processes. We examine possible biases arising from single-aperture and integrated measurements and find that, while they can under- or over-estimate attenuation and SFRs for individual galaxies, the sample-averaged trends remain roughly unchanged, with the derived SFRs consistent with the star-forming main sequence, and a small scatter. From our sample, we find a median stellar-to-nebular reddening ratio f = E(B-V)$_{\rm star}$/E(B-V)$_{\rm gas}$ of 0.88 with an interquartile range of 0.51-0.96, suggesting relatively uniform dust distributions even in intermediate-mass galaxies (stellar masses $\sim 10^9$-$10^{10.5}~M_{\odot}$). Our results highlight the importance of spatially resolved attenuation measurements for accurately tracing star formation and understanding the evolving dust geometry in galaxies during a critical epoch of morphological transformation.
papers.Reasons for match: This paper uses JWST/NIRSpec spatially resolved spectroscopy of z~1 star-forming galaxies to study dust attenuation, relevant to my interests in JWST spectroscopy, SED fitting, dust attenuation, and galaxy evolution.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks how dust attenuation profiles vary radially in main-sequence galaxies at z~1. It finds diverse radial attenuation profiles, with most flat or positive, and a median stellar-to-nebular reddening ratio of 0.88. This matters for interpreting JWST spectra and SEDs of high-redshift galaxies, especially for dust correction and star formation rate estimates.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for the radial attenuation profile measurements and their dependence on stellar mass
Check how single-aperture versus spatially resolved SFRs compare
Check the Balmer decrement methodology and assumptions
Look for any discussion of implications for higher-redshift JWST samples

papers.title: Reconstructing the Projected Dark Matter Field across 0.1-100 Mpc Scales from the SDSS Survey
papers.authors: Kunyao Zhao , Yingjie Peng , Dingyi Zhao , Xiaohu Yang , Luis C. Ho , Kai Wang , Jing Dou , Zeyu Gao , Qiusheng Gu , Yukun Liu , Roberto Maiolino , Houjun Mo , Alvio Renzini , Canpo Su , Bitao Wang , Yu-Chen Wang , Bingxiao Xu , Feng Yuan , Xingye Zhu
papers.abstract: Dark matter sets the gravitational environment in which galaxies form and evolve, but cannot be observed directly. We present a conditional diffusion model that reconstructs the projected dark matter density field from the galaxy stellar-mass density field for direct application to galaxy surveys. The model is trained on CAMELS and validated on the independent IllustrisTNG300-1 simulation. Halo masses inferred from the reconstructed projected-aperture measurements agree well with the corresponding true values, with a scatter below 0.2 dex. On 100 kpc scales, reconstructed surface densities show a typical scatter of ~0.3 dex in the regime most relevant for observations. We apply the model to SDSS galaxies with $M_\star\ge10^9\,M_\odot$ in a contiguous low-redshift region. Averaging over 100 stochastic realizations, we reconstruct and publicly release a projected dark matter field covering $90\times90\,(h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc})^2$ with a pixel size of $0.097\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$. This pixel area corresponds to the characteristic projected area of halos with masses of ~$10^{10.6}\,h^{-1}\,M_\odot$. The map reveals the multiscale projected cosmic web, including cluster-scale overdensities, filaments and voids. Projected-aperture masses are statistically consistent with SDSS group-catalog masses, while the derived halo mass function broadly matches mock-catalog expectations. The reconstructed projected potential places Coma in one of the deepest wells and near a convergence region of the inferred projected acceleration field, suggesting that the reconstruction retains both local overdensities and coherent large-scale projected gravitational structure. This work shows that diffusion-based dark matter reconstruction can be applied to real galaxy surveys, enabling halo-mass- and spatially resolved dark-matter-environment-based studies of galaxy evolution in SDSS and future wide-area surveys.
papers.Reasons for match: This is a machine-learning dark matter reconstruction paper applied to SDSS, relevant to AI-for-astronomy and galaxy evolution but not directly to JWST high-redshift AGN or LRDs.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks whether a conditional diffusion model can reconstruct the projected dark matter field from galaxy stellar mass density. It validates the method on simulations and applies it to SDSS, releasing a projected dark matter map. This matters for my work mainly as an example of AI-based inference for galaxy surveys, potentially adaptable to high-z environments.
Full-text inspection checklist: Check whether the diffusion model framework could be adapted to JWST survey fields
Look for validation metrics and scatter that indicate reliability
Check whether the method accounts for AGN or non-stellar mass contributions
Look for any discussion of high-redshift applicability
